name: Ace Hardware
desc: Retailer-owned co-operative supplying and branding thousands of independently owned hardware stores in the United States and abroad.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 9.17bn in 2022 (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: Over 5,700 locations, mainly across the United States, plus international stores such as in the Maldives.
rationale: Large national retail brand with marketing scale; F1's fast-growing US fan base could support store traffic and co-operative brand awareness.

name: Amy's Kitchen
desc: Family-owned American maker of organic and non-GMO frozen meals, soups and convenience foods sold internationally.
capacity_detail: Revenue reportedly over USD 500M a year in 2017, per Wikipedia
markets: Sells in the United States, the United Kingdom and France, expanding in Asia and Australia.
rationale: Natural-food brand expanding abroad; F1 hospitality and sustainability messaging could reach health-conscious international consumers, though fit is modest.

name: Barton Malow
desc: Family-controlled American construction firm providing general contracting, construction management and design-build services nationwide.
capacity_detail: Reported revenue USD 4.4bn in 2026 (Wikipedia infobox and text, ENR ranking)
markets: Construction projects across the United States, including sports venues, industrial, healthcare and education facilities.
rationale: Builds sports and entertainment venues; F1 hospitality could support business development with US developers and Las Vegas or Miami race stakeholders.

name: Brasfield & Gorrie
desc: Privately held construction firm in Birmingham, Alabama, offering general contracting, design-build and construction management across many markets.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 6.37bn in 2024 (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: Construction projects mainly across the southeastern United States, in healthcare, commercial, industrial and other markets.
rationale: B2B contractor with little consumer marketing; F1 hospitality could serve client entertainment, but relevance is limited.

name: CKE Restaurants
desc: Owner and franchisor of the Carl's Jr. and Hardee's fast-food burger chains in the United States and abroad.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 1.28bn in 2012 (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: Carl's Jr. and Hardee's restaurants in the United States and franchised international markets.
rationale: Bold-advertising burger brand with international franchises; F1's young US audience fits Carl's Jr. marketing style.

name: Church's Texas Chicken
desc: American fried chicken restaurant chain operating as Church's Chicken and Texas Chicken in the United States and abroad.
ownership: private equity: High Bluff Capital Partners
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 1.6bn in 2025 (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: United States, Puerto Rico, Canada, Mexico, the Caribbean, the Gulf, Egypt, Germany, Southeast Asia and New Zealand.
rationale: International quick-service brand trading as Texas Chicken abroad; F1 races in Asia and the Middle East overlap its franchise markets.

name: Consigli Construction
desc: Employee-owned construction manager and general contractor in Milford, Massachusetts, building across the northeastern United States.
capacity_detail: Upward of USD 4.4bn in annual volume, current (company history page, undated)
markets: Construction projects in the northeastern and mid-Atlantic United States.
rationale: B2B contractor with limited consumer marketing; F1 hospitality might help client relationships but relevance is low.

name: DPR Construction
desc: Employee-owned American general contractor specializing in technology, life sciences, healthcare, education and commercial office projects.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 10.8bn in 2024 (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: 32 offices; works in the United States, South Korea, Singapore and Europe (Benelux, DACH and Nordic regions).
rationale: Builds data centres for technology firms already in F1; hospitality could deepen relationships with those tech clients.

name: E. & J. Gallo Winery
desc: Largest family-owned winery in the United States, producing California wines under more than one hundred labels.
capacity_detail: Annual revenue of USD 5.3bn reported (Wikipedia; year not stated)
markets: Wines distributed internationally, including a UK business, with brands sold across the United States and abroad.
rationale: Global wine brand owner; rival drinks groups use F1 for premium positioning, and Gallo could do the same for its luxury labels.

name: Epic Systems
desc: Privately held American healthcare software company developing electronic health record systems for hospitals and medical groups.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 6.7bn in 2025 (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: Hospitals and health systems in the United States and other countries, with cloud hosting on Google Cloud.
rationale: Large software firm, but sells to hospitals and avoids brand advertising; F1 fit is weak.

name: Esri
desc: Privately held American developer of ArcGIS geographic information system mapping and spatial analytics software used worldwide.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 1.1bn in 2014 (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: Users in every country, with offices and over 3,000 partners worldwide.
rationale: Global mapping software brand; F1's data and track-mapping story could showcase ArcGIS, as rival software firms do in F1.

name: Fabletics
desc: American subscription activewear brand selling athletic apparel online and through more than seventy retail stores.
capacity_detail: Surpassed USD 500M annual revenue in 2020 (Wikipedia)
sponsorships: Varsity Spirit apparel partner (2018-2024); Tough Mudder partner (2021); Hydrow apparel partner
markets: Online subscription sales and over 72 stores, mainly in the United States.
rationale: Celebrity-led activewear brand seeking reach; F1's young, fashion-minded audience suits its lifestyle marketing.

name: Family Dollar
desc: American chain of discount variety stores selling groceries and household goods at low prices across the United States.
ownership: private equity: Brigade Capital Management and Macellum Capital Management
capacity_detail: Sold by Dollar Tree to Brigade Capital Management and Macellum Capital for USD 1bn (agreed March 2025, completed July 2025)
markets: Discount stores across the United States except Alaska and Hawaii.
rationale: Mass-market US discount retailer; F1's premium positioning is a poor match beyond US fan reach.

name: Fisher Investments
desc: Independent American money management firm serving private clients and institutions, managing over USD 400 billion in assets.
capacity_detail: Valued at USD 12.75bn when Advent International and ADIA completed a USD 3bn minority investment (Jan 2025)
markets: 29 offices; serves clients in the United States, Canada, Europe, the Middle East, Asia and Australasia.
rationale: Wealth manager targeting affluent investors; F1 hospitality and brand reach in the US and Europe match its client base, as rivals sponsor.

name: Forever Living Products
desc: American multi-level marketing company founded by Rex Maughan, selling aloe vera based products through independent distributors.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 4bn in 2022 (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: Network of about 9.3 million distributors selling in many countries worldwide.
rationale: Global distributor network brand; F1 visibility could support recruitment and incentive trips, though MLM reputation limits fit.

name: Golden State Foods
desc: Foodservice manufacturer and distributor supplying sauces, proteins and logistics to quick-service restaurant chains such as McDonald's.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 5.1bn in 2022 (estimate, Wikipedia infobox citing LA Daily News)
markets: Serves restaurant chains in the United States and internationally from manufacturing and distribution centres.
rationale: B2B supplier with no consumer brand; F1 relevance is low beyond client hospitality.

name: Goya Foods
desc: Family-owned American producer of Hispanic and Latin American foods such as beans, rice, sauces and spices.
capacity_detail: More than USD 1bn annual revenue by 2004; infobox revenue USD 1.5bn (no year)
markets: United States, Puerto Rico, Dominican Republic, Spain and Hispanic markets worldwide.
rationale: Leading Hispanic food brand; F1 races in Miami, Mexico and Spain could reach its Latin consumers.

name: Guess
desc: American fashion brand designing and selling clothing, denim and accessories through stores, licensees and online worldwide.
ownership: private, Authentic Brands Group (51% of IP) with Marciano founders
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 2.99bn in 2025 (Wikipedia infobox, from FY2025 annual report)
markets: About 1,600 locations worldwide through stores, licensees and online channels.
rationale: Glamour-led global fashion brand recently taken private; F1's lifestyle audience in Europe and Asia mirrors Guess customers, as Tommy Hilfiger shows.

name: Hallmark Cards
desc: Family-owned American maker of greeting cards, gifts and keepsakes, also owning the Hallmark television channels.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 5.0bn in 2020 (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: Greeting cards and gifts sold across the United States and internationally, plus US cable channels.
rationale: Strong consumer brand with media assets, but family-oriented positioning offers limited fit with F1.

name: Hensel Phelps
desc: Employee-owned American general contractor and construction manager delivering airports, government, healthcare and commercial projects nationwide.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 8.2bn in 2025 (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: Construction projects across the United States, including airports and government facilities.
rationale: B2B contractor with low consumer marketing; F1 hospitality could aid client relations, but relevance is low.

name: In-N-Out Burger
desc: Family-owned American fast-food chain serving burgers, fries and shakes from restaurants in the western and southern United States.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 1.823bn in FY2022 (Wikipedia infobox citing Restaurant Business Top 500)
markets: About 424 restaurants in the western and southern United States.
rationale: Cult US brand with car-culture roots; F1's Las Vegas race sits in its heartland, though it rarely advertises.

name: J.Crew
desc: American clothing retailer selling men's and women's apparel, shoes and accessories under J.Crew and Madewell brands.
ownership: private equity: Anchorage Capital Group and Leonard Green & Partners
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 2.54bn in 2019 (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: Stores and online sales mainly in the United States, plus Nordstrom wholesale.
rationale: Preppy US fashion brand; F1 lifestyle content could reach affluent American shoppers, but international reach is limited.

name: King's Hawaiian
desc: Family-owned American bakery known for Hawaiian sweet rolls sold through US grocery retailers and restaurants.
capacity_detail: NASCAR Cup Series sponsor: Joe Gibbs Racing and Denny Hamlin from 2025 (multi-year deal), after RFK Racing 2022-2024
sponsorships: Joe Gibbs Racing NASCAR Cup (2025-); RFK Racing NASCAR Cup (2022-2024)
markets: Sold through grocery stores across the United States.
rationale: Already funds NASCAR Cup sponsorship; F1's growing US audience offers a motorsport extension, though its reach is mainly domestic.

name: Clayco
desc: Privately owned American real estate, architecture, engineering, design-build and construction firm delivering large commercial and industrial projects.
capacity_detail: Revenue of USD 8.1bn+ for 2025 (company overview page)
markets: Design-build and construction projects across the United States.
rationale: Large B2B builder with limited consumer marketing; F1 hospitality could support client relations, but relevance is low.

name: HP Hood
desc: Independently owned American dairy company producing milk, cream, ice cream and cultured dairy products under Hood and licensed brands.
capacity_detail: Annual sales revenue of over USD 3bn (Wikipedia text; infobox USD 3.5bn); #169 on Forbes America's Largest Private Companies 2025
markets: Dairy products sold across the United States, with a strong base in New England.
rationale: Regional dairy brand with mainly domestic sales; F1 fit is weak beyond US fan engagement.

name: Hendrick Automotive Group
desc: Largest privately held automotive retail organisation in the United States, operating new-car dealerships and collision centres.
capacity_detail: Revenue over USD 13.6bn in 2025 (company corporate page)
markets: 103 dealerships across 13 US states, plus 22 collision centres.
rationale: Motorsport-rooted dealer group tied to Hendrick Motorsports; F1's US growth and Cadillac's entry could suit its premium dealerships.
